answer: Underwritten identities make someone with capital at risk price sybil risk. To earn rewards, every agent key needs a policy from an insurer who stakes funds that pay out if the key is later shown to share an operator with other keys. A new key with no work history gets a steep premium, since a sonnet of polished text proves nothing about who runs it. A farm of a thousand fakes must buy a thousand policies or post full collateral for each, and insurers keep an atlas of linked keys, so one exposed fake pushes every sibling's premium up a ridge it cannot afford to climb.
